scenes.head: Fractional or full‑time CFO?
scenes.sub: Start with what your board needs every month.
scenes.say: Fractional or full-time CFO? Don't start with the job title. Start with what your board needs every month.

scenes.desc: after the tax period ends, to file and pay (general rule). For a 31 Dec 2026 year‑end: 30 Sep 2027.
scenes.src: Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022, Articles 48 and 53; FTA release of 26 Sep 2026; the FTA may set another date. Checked 23 Oct 2026.
scenes.say: Here's one example. In the UAE, a taxable person generally files the corporate tax return, and pays, within nine months of the end of the tax period. For a December twenty twenty-six year-end, that points to the thirtieth of September, twenty twenty-seven.

items.l: One monthly pack the board can rely on
A forward view, not last month's balance
Tax, lender and licence dates planned early

scenes.say: So ask three questions. Are the monthly numbers final by a fixed date? Can you see your cash three months ahead? And does one person own every filing date?

items.small: A few days a month, when the board needs the pack, the cash view and the calendar
When finance decisions come up daily: several entities, active financing, a large team

scenes.say: If that's what your board needs, a few days a month of CFO-level support can often cover it. If finance decisions come up every day, across several entities or lenders, a full-time hire starts to make sense.
